notes: Single university-level document. Many units are general integrity rules (cheating, fabrication, collaboration, crediting) that do not name AI; coded with fit_note. Dropped one coder-A unit ('without permission from the instructor' as P06) as an exact repeat of the permission condition already coded in the AI-on-assessments and AI-submitted-work units.

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy for Undergraduate Students (Navigating Artificial Intelligence)
documents.stance_why: Coder A said restrict, coder B delegates. The page makes 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' plagiarism and bars AI on assessments and as submitted work 'without permission from the instructor' or 'contrary to instructions from the instructor'. It offers no tiers; AI is barred unless the instructor permits, which is restrict. Instructors grant the permission but the document itself sets the default ban.
documents.summary: The Provost's undergraduate academic integrity page folds AI into its definitions of misconduct. Using AI tools on assessments, submitting substantially AI-produced work, or using AI against instructor instructions without permission counts as plagiarism. It has no AI-specific permissions, disclosure rules or sanctions; instructors decide what is allowed.

units.why: The opening sentence classes 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' as plagiarism and so as academic misconduct, which is the integrity-process classification (P36), not a stance rule.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor student, unit_stance restrict; coder B: actor all, unit_stance prohibit. The source lists 'unauthorized use of artificial intelligence' among misconduct 'prohibited behaviors for students', so the rule binds students; only unauthorized use is misconduct, so restrict rather than prohibit. Type P36 agreed.
units.anchor: plagiarism (including unauthorized use of artificial intelligence)

units.why: Points students to the Academic Integrity Policy and Student Conduct Code: 'Please review the WashU Academic Integrity Policy'. A pointer to further rules, so P115 rather than P78 since it names documents, not course rules.

units.why: Defines cheating to include 'use of any unauthorized assistance' in assessments; AI is not named but the rule covers it as unauthorized assistance, and it bans unauthorized aid on exams. P22 fits partly because AI is not named.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: unit_stance prohibit; coder B: restrict. The source bans 'unauthorized assistance', so assistance is barred only when not authorized, which is restrict. AI is not named; both coders flagged fit.
units.anchor: use of any unauthorized assistance or source in taking quizzes, tests, examinations
units.fit_note: Does not name AI; bans any unauthorized assistance or source on assessments, which covers AI by implication.

units.why: Cheating includes 'sources beyond those authorized by the instructor in writing' for assignments, so the instructor decides which aids are allowed; this is instructor-set authorization (P04), and by default unauthorized sources are barred.
units.anchor: use of or referral to sources beyond those authorized by the instructor in writing
units.fit_note: Generic sources rule, not AI-specific; also implies a restrictive default unless the instructor authorizes.

units.why: Plagiarism defined as 'unacknowledged use of materials prepared by another person' or a company; AI is not named, so this is the general acknowledgment duty. Closest is P24 (acknowledge use), though only partly.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. Source (plagiarism clause ii) lists 'unacknowledged use of materials prepared by another person' as a rule separate from the citation clause; a real rule, kept with its fit note (not AI-specific).
units.anchor: unacknowledged use of materials prepared by another person
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI; general duty to credit others' work, which the AI section builds on.

units.why: The policy lists 'use of artificial intelligence tools' on 'quizzes, tests, examinations, or other assessments without permission from the instructor' as misconduct; AI is banned on assessments unless the instructor permits, which is P22.
units.anchor: use of artificial intelligence tools or other tools that generate artificial content in taking quizzes

units.why: Submitting work 'produced in material or substantial part through use of artificial intelligence tools' without permission is misconduct. This is the not-have-AI-produce-your-work rule (P19), with a permission exception.
units.anchor: submitting work for evaluation as one’s own that was produced in material or substantial part
units.fit_note: The ban is tied to 'material or substantial part' and to missing instructor permission, so minor or permitted AI help is not barred.

units.why: Using AI 'in a manner contrary to instructions from the instructor' is misconduct, so the instructor's instructions set the AI rule, which is per-instructor control (P04).
units.anchor: in a manner contrary to instructions from the instructor

units.why: Item (iv) makes AI use that violates 'any other provision of these rules concerning academic dishonesty' misconduct, so AI is held to all existing integrity rules; this is P77 (comply with existing policy).
units.resolution_why: Coder A: phase when-misuse; coder B: general. Clause (iv) defines a further category of misconduct ('violates any other provision of these rules concerning academic dishonesty'), the same misconduct classification as the P36 unit, so when-misuse. Type P77 and must-not agreed.
units.anchor: in a manner that violates any other provision of these rules concerning academic dishonesty

units.why: The unauthorized-AI definition applies to 'tools that generate artificial content' broadly, extending beyond named AI tools; it defines the scope of what counts, so P61.
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder A. Source defines unauthorized AI as 'artificial intelligence tools or other tools that generate artificial content', which sets the scope of covered tools; a real definition, kept as P61 with its fit note.
units.anchor: artificial intelligence tools or other tools that generate artificial content
units.fit_note: No standalone definition; scope is set inside the misconduct definition.

units.why: Fabrication or falsification of data or records is listed as misconduct, e.g. 'altering, omitting or inventing laboratory data'. AI is not mentioned; this is a general ban on fabrication, so P74 as the nearest type.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P74 but anchored different passages (A: lab data alteration in the Fabrication section; B: 'fabrication or falsification of data or records' in the intro list). Same rule, merged using A's more specific anchor; phase during-work (work submitted as findings), not general. Not AI-specific.
units.anchor: altering, omitting or inventing laboratory data to submit as one’s own findings

units.why: Other misconduct: 'Submit any academic work under someone else’s name other than one’s own'. A general own-work rule not specific to AI; closest is P29.

units.why: A student's name on work 'is a written statement that credit for the work belongs to that student alone', and collaborators must be acknowledged; this is the own-what-you-submit rule (P29).

units.why: 'Unless the instructor explicitly states otherwise, it is dishonest to collaborate' sets a restrictive default with an instructor exception, covering writing computer programs; not AI-specific, nearest is P06 (fallback when silent).

units.why: When group work is allowed only in some cases, 'it is the student’s responsibility to understand the degree of acceptable collaboration' and ask for clarification; this is the student duty to learn and follow the rules (P78), with ask-first element of P10.
units.resolution_why: Coder A: P78, must, course-start; coder B: P10, should, during-work. The anchor 'it is the student's responsibility to understand the degree of acceptable collaboration' states a duty to know the rules, which is P78 and must; the ask-for-clarification part is outside the anchor. The understanding is needed 'for each assignment', so during-work.
